reason: The claim checks out. main() (ladder_watch.py l.899-904) catches only KeyboardInterrupt, and run() (l.699-742) has no try/except inside its loop. save_state (l.415-418) calls os.replace, and I reproduced the failure on this machine: open(state.json) in the same process gives PermissionError 13, and a second process reading in a tight loop made 3076 of 4432 replaces fail. Other unhandled paths: any KeyError/TypeError in resolve_event/evaluate, and a print to a closed stdout pipe. Only the CLI subprocess and load_lb are fail-soft. A realistic reader holds state.json for about 1 ms per read against a 120-300 s save interval, so this exact collision is unlikely. The bigger risk is that the watcher has never run live: only the dry run and 35 unit tests. By R13-A1 (3), a dead watcher DROPS the A-only extension. This is local read-only tooling, not a kernel stage or a new mechanism, so R8 and the byte-identical rule do not apply, and it needs no submit. The --s0 file is valid: imported into a scratch dir it gives count 40, rank 242, 0.954, 241 TeamIds above. Two corrections to the finding. Fix (B) as written (catch in main, save, return 1) still ENDS the process, so on its own it does not keep the extension alive. Fix (A) also restarts after Ctrl-C (rc 130).
fix: Use (A) as the primary fix. Launch it from an independent terminal, not a Claude Code background task that may die with its session, and use sleep 120 rather than 60: until python experiments/lb_poll/ladder_watch.py --s0 experiments/e10_watch/20260927T0147Z.txt --hard-cap 2026-09-27T11:30Z >> experiments/lb_poll/ladder_watch.stdout.log 2>&1; do sleep 120; done. Stop it with the PAUSE file or by killing the loop. Optional hardening: in save_state, retry os.replace up to 5 times with a 0.2 s sleep, catching OSError; if all 5 fail, log and continue (state.json is only for resume). In run(), wrap each loop iteration in except Exception: write the traceback to watch.log, sleep SLOW_S, continue. Do not use a main()-level catch that returns. After the edit, rerun tests/test_ladder_watch.py and --dry-run. Tell round-15 agents to read only watch.log and calls.jsonl, never state.json.
realistic_gain: No direct score change: this only protects the conditional A-only finals swap (exp70a for #37). That swap has a low chance of firing. By the L1 prior, P(exp70a > #37) is about 0.20, and exp70e and exp70a were submitted 2 min apart, so they will probably complete together; with equal displays that makes both refs NEU, so no attributable UP. The chance of a crash is also low but not zero. The cost is about 2 minutes, so it is worth doing before 04:10Z.
